items.title: HRF condemns Vizag police curbs on campaigns against hyperscale data centres
items.summary: Follow TNM's WhatsApp channel for news updates and story links. The Human Rights Forum (HRF) has condemned the Visakhapatnam police for preventing citizens from peacefully campaigning against the establishment of massive data centres in the city. On Sunday, August 9, which marked the anniversary of the Quit India movement, members of a group called Green Visakha had called for a procession on the Vizag beach road to spread awareness on the potential environmental impact of hyperscale artificial intelligence (AI) data centres. While police had earlier denied permission for the event, around 25 people gathered at the Bhagat Singh statue, and police arrived and objected to the small gathering too, HRF said. The Andhra Pradesh government has announced that it has entered agreements with various companies to establish data centres with a capacity of around nine gigawatts near Vizag. “The campaign aimed to confront serious questions arising from the sheer scale and concentration of these projects.
